response:
Evidence diagnosis. The archive's best signal is MIN(z(che/lct), z(GP/at)) (fmb 3.54, alpha +4.7%, t 4.03). But two follow-ups constrain its interpretation: the imbalance term ABS(gap) was null (fmb -0.58, alpha 0.002), which means MIN ≈ average of the two legs plus a term with no independent pricing content, and adding a leverage leg (Triple) *weakened* everything (sharpe -0.01). Separately, rank-times-z conditional structures repeatedly split the metrics: GrossProfitCoverageOfNearTermClaims got fmb 2.99 with alpha t 1.11, while MarginRepairUnderLiquidityStress got both aligned (fmb 2.36, alpha t 2.06). So this batch (i) settles whether the min is truly non-additive, (ii) tests the scaling of the two coverage legs, (iii) extends the one conditional channel that worked on both metrics, and (iv) opens two genuinely new distress channels (operating-cycle deterioration and within-firm liquidity lows).

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: CoverageWeakestLinkStockVersusFlow
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(che, lct)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), lct)))
HYPOTHESIS: Near-term claims can be met from a stock of cash or from the flow of gross profit, and since these resources cover the same obligations they are complements at the margin: the firm's expected return is set by whichever coverage source is weaker relative to the claims it faces.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This isolates one design choice in the archive winner — scaling the quality leg by current liabilities (a coverage concept) instead of total assets (a profitability concept) — so both legs are denominated in the same obligations and the minimum becomes an economically literal binding constraint rather than a mix of a coverage ratio and a profitability ratio. If it improves both fmb_tstat and alpha, the mechanism is claim coverage; if it degrades, the gross-profitability premium was doing the work.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: RecoveryTrendWithinBindingDistress
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(NEG(MIN(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(che, lct)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at))))), IND_ZSCORE(TREND(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: The weakest-link score identifies which firms are actually constrained; among those firms, the direction of gross profitability decides whether the constraint is relaxing or tightening, so improving multi-year gross profitability earns large abnormal returns precisely where the binding constraint is tight and deteriorating profitability is punished hardest there.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This uses the archive winner as a conditioning variable rather than as a predictor, converting a static state measure into a state-times-direction interaction that no single-theme signal can express. The magnitude leg is non-negative (distress intensity) and the sign leg is a centered trend, giving a two-sided spread concentrated in the constrained subsample instead of re-sorting on the level premium already documented.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: CostRatioTrendUnderLiquidityStress
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(NEG(RATIO(che, lct))), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(TREND(RATIO(cogs, revt), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: Sustained improvement in unit costs, not a single noisy annual change, is what tells investors that a liquidity-stressed firm is repairing its operating model; a multi-year downward trend in cost-of-goods intensity under liquidity stress predicts recovery while a persistent upward trend predicts funding failure.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The one-year version of this channel produced aligned but modest evidence (fmb 2.36, alpha t 2.06), and the natural diagnosis is measurement noise in single-year cogs/revt changes for low-revenue firms, which a three-year trend attenuates. This is a deliberate horizon isolation on the only conditional channel in the archive whose two metrics agreed.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: WorkingCapitalBuildWithMarginDecay
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(wcap, revt), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: A ballooning working-capital position relative to revenue means inventory is not selling and receivables are not collecting; that build is benign when margins are holding but signals impending distress when it coincides with margin decay, because the firm is financing unsold output while its unit economics erode.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This is an operating-cycle deterioration channel that no archive signal touches: the distress dimension is the change in the working-capital stock per unit of revenue, and the quality dimension is the contemporaneous direction of gross margin, so the signal fires only for the toxic combination and reverses sign for firms building working capital while margins expand (a growth, not distress, state). Both legs are changes, so the construct is orthogonal to the level-based composites already tested.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: OwnHistoryLiquidityLowWithIntactMargins
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(che, lct), 5))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Distress is partly a within-firm event: a firm sitting at the bottom of its own five-year liquidity range is under transient funding stress, and if its gross profitability is intact that stress is temporary and mean-reverting, whereas the same within-firm liquidity low with weak gross profitability marks structural decline.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every archive signal measures distress cross-sectionally, so within-firm liquidity position is a new information axis that automatically neutralizes stable firm- and industry-level differences in optimal cash holdings. The centered gross-profitability leg supplies the sign, so the prediction is explicitly conditional: liquidity depletion is good news for profitable firms and bad news for unprofitable ones.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: AdditiveSolvencyBenchmark
EXPRESSION: ADD(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(che, lct)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: If liquidity and gross profitability are substitutable contributors to solvency, their industry-standardized sum should price expected returns as well as their minimum, and the archive winner's performance would then be a two-premium composite rather than a complementarity effect.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The null result on the absolute-gap term already implies MIN is close to this sum, so measuring the sum directly with identical legs quantifies exactly how much the non-substitutable structure contributes and is the decisive diagnostic for where to spend the remaining generations. If the additive version matches or beats the minimum, we should abandon min-family refinements and concentrate on the conditional dynamics channels; if it is clearly weaker, the complementarity is real and worth deepening.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---CRITIQUE CoverageWeakestLinkStockVersusFlow---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: This is a single-denominator swap on the archive winner (at → lct in the quality leg) using a ratio already deployed in GrossProfitCoverageOfNearTermClaims, so despite the coherent "common-denominator coverage" framing it is a near-cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different mechanism.

---CRITIQUE RecoveryTrendWithinBindingDistress---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Repurposing the weakest-link score as a non-negative conditioning intensity and letting a centered multi-year gross-profitability trend supply the sign is a genuine state×direction interaction with internally consistent sign logic, though it will need to be checked against a plain profitability-trend baseline to prove the conditioning adds anything.

---CRITIQUE CostRatioTrendUnderLiquidityStress---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This differs from the archive's MarginRepairUnderLiquidityStress only by swapping lt→lct and DELTA(1)→TREND(3), which is a horizon/scaling tweak of an already-tested channel rather than a new economic mechanism.

---CRITIQUE WorkingCapitalBuildWithMarginDecay---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The construction and expected negative sign are internally consistent and the change-on-change design is orthogonal to the archive's level composites, but the distress leg (scaled change in working capital) is essentially the working-capital accruals anomaly, so the test must demonstrate that the margin-decay interaction adds incremental power beyond a plain accruals sort.

---CRITIQUE OwnHistoryLiquidityLowWithIntactMargins---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The within-firm liquidity axis is a legitimately new information dimension for this archive, but because the RANK leg is non-negative the signal is mechanically a reweighted gross-profitability premium and risks rediscovering Novy-Marx unless the depletion interaction is shown to matter on its own.

---CRITIQUE AdditiveSolvencyBenchmark---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: A plain sum of two industry-standardized, individually well-known premia (cash-to-current-liabilities and gross profitability) is too trivial to count as a cross-theme signal and is best run as an offline control regression rather than consuming an evaluation slot.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: RolloverGapAgainstInternalFunds
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, ADD(che, SUB(revt, cogs))), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: Distress is triggered by maturity, not by leverage: what matters is how much debt comes due within the year relative to the funds the firm can generate internally, namely cash on hand plus one year of gross profit. Firms whose maturing obligations exceed their internal funding capacity must access external markets on someone else's terms and earn low subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Debt maturity structure is an information axis absent from the entire archive, which has measured distress only through liquidity ratios, total-liability burdens, and loss states, so this is a new channel rather than a denominator swap. The interaction is intrinsic: the numerator is a distress-side claim with a hard deadline and the denominator is a quality-side internal funding flow plus stock, and neither side alone defines the refinancing gap that the mechanism prices.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: EarningsTroughWithFlexibleCostBase
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(pi, at), 5))), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(RATIO(dp, ADD(cogs, dp)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Operating leverage matters asymmetrically: for a firm sitting at the bottom of its own five-year pretax-earnings range, a largely variable cost base (low depreciation share of the operating cost base) allows it to shrink and survive the trough, while a rigid, capacity-heavy cost base converts the same trough into permanent value destruction.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Cost rigidity previously entered only as a level channel inside a static minimum and was weak, which is consistent with rigidity being irrelevant in normal times and decisive only in downturns — exactly the state-dependence this conditional design tests rather than re-tests. The distress axis is a within-firm earnings drawdown, so the signal is not a cross-sectional profitability sort, and the centered rigidity leg gives a two-sided spread inside the trough group.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: TaxValidatedEarningsUnderLiquidityStress
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(NEG(RATIO(che, lct))), SUB(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(txt, revt)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(pi, revt))))
HYPOTHESIS: When liquidity is thin, the credibility of reported profits determines survival: a cash-poor firm whose tax burden is high relative to its reported book profitability is earning income the tax authority also recognizes, whereas a cash-poor firm reporting book profits with an unusually light tax burden is reporting accounting income that will not service obligations.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The signed leg is the tax-versus-book profitability divergence, not a tax level, so it cannot collapse into the profitability premium the way txt/revt alone would — a firm with high margins and correspondingly high taxes scores neutrally, and only the mismatch is priced. Conditioning on liquidity stress supplies the distress interaction: earnings credibility is second-order for cash-rich firms and first-order for firms that must convert reported profits into cash immediately.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
